mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and increases present value of future earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions and impending economic slowdown, depressing corporate earnings and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.4pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) over the past two months indicates broad-based demand contraction, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% and RSAFS declines > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by the specified thresholds, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, indicating supply-side contraction, the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to suppressed corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it reflects a robust labor market supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS is above 150,000, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1700 thousand units over the past two months signals weakening housing market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as a leading indicator of economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 1700, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 290) over the past month indicates active monetary easing in a low-inflation environment, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines > 0.1pp and CPIAUCSL < 290, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annualized growth rate below 2.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth expectations as the economy approaches a slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate < 2.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.02.
